text.en:
Arun's lunchbox had only biscuits. Priya's had rice, dal, a vegetable and a fruit.
"Why do you eat so many things?" asked Arun.
"My body needs different foods to grow, play and stay well," said Priya.

Food gives us energy and helps us grow and stay healthy. The useful parts of food are called nutrients.
Carbohydrates (rice, wheat, potato) give energy. Proteins (dal, eggs, milk, fish) help the body grow and repair. Fats (oil, ghee, nuts) give a lot of energy.
Vitamins and minerals (fruits, vegetables, milk) protect the body from disease. Fibre (whole grains, vegetables) helps us pass waste. Water is also needed.
A balanced diet has all nutrients in the right amounts. Eating only one kind of food, or too much junk food, is not healthy.
Mindful eating means eating slowly, chewing well, not wasting food and washing hands before eating.
Food gives energy and helps us grow. The useful parts of food are nutrients.
Carbohydrates and fats give energy. Proteins help us grow and repair.
Vitamins and minerals protect us from disease. Fibre helps digestion.
A balanced diet has all the nutrients. Eat slowly, chew well and do not waste food.

problem.en: Which nutrient is missing from a meal of only rice and oil, and which foods can add it?

text.en: Rice gives carbohydrates and oil gives fats.
Proteins, vitamins and minerals are missing.

why.en: The meal has no dal, vegetable or fruit.

text.en: We can add dal for protein and vegetables and a fruit for vitamins and minerals.

why.en: Now the meal is more balanced.

prompt.en: A friend eats only chips and sweets every day. What will you tell him?

requiredIdeas.en: His body needs all nutrients in the right amounts.
He should add dal, vegetables, fruit and milk and eat less junk food.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking tasty food is the same as healthy food.

points.en: Nutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.
A balanced diet has all of them.
Eat slowly and do not waste food.
